cases.title: First lesson: asks what should snap before proposing; candidates as questions, at most three; real names

rubric.reason: The reply opens with a real question, 'In Mentor Practice 2, is anything meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?', before it names any candidate or sets a focus.

Only two candidates are named, both by layer and property, and each is a question ('Is it meant to snap on and off instead?', 'Is that meant to snap, or to fade?'); neither is called a mistake and there is no instruction to hold.
Every name and time comes from the snapshot: Mentor Practice 2, Blink/Opacity with first_time 1 and 3 pairs, Cut/Opacity with first_time 3 and 1 pair, and Seal left out as a precomp.

The mentor sets no focus and gives no instruction to hold; it frames Blink and Cut as questions ('Is either one meant to snap instead?') and ends with the real intent question 'So is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off or a cut?'

Only two candidates are named, Blink's Opacity and Cut's Opacity; 'Right now they both fade between their keys' is stated neutrally rather than as a mistake, followed by 'Is either one meant to snap instead?', with no instruction to hold.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity at 1 s with three pairs, Cut Opacity at 3 s with one pair, and Seal as a precomp all match the key_types_snapshot result (comp.name, candidates, left_out).
